clean_story:
Unimaginable speed. Cosmic energy.

The name Oh My God Particule comes from the exclamation of the scientist who first detected it in 1991, as its energy was so extreme it defied expectations. It is a subatomic particle, likely a proton, traveling at nearly the speed of light, carrying the kinetic energy of a baseball pitched at one hundred kilometers per hour—compressed into a single particle smaller than an atom. No human-made accelerator can replicate such energy. The particle’s origin remains unknown, though theories suggest it may come from violent cosmic events like quasars or gamma-ray bursts. Detectors like the Fly’s Eye in Utah captured its trace, revealing a path so straight it implied no magnetic field in the galaxy could bend it. This particle challenges our understanding of physics, as no known source in our universe should be able to produce it.

Three related subjects are cosmic rays, ultra-high-energy particles and dark matter.
